title: Prescribing Under a Massachusetts Collaborative Practice Agreement
topic: Collaborative practice / Prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement
subtopic: The three-fold power in the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G), the purpose-specific Department registration in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2), the additional conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) where prescriptive practices are included, the particulars supplied to a dispensing pharmacist under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), and the facility medication order in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8)
learning_objectives: State the three acts the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorise and explain why authority to do one of them is not authority to do another.
Explain what the proviso closing the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) does to the numbered paragraphs that follow it.
Apply the purpose element in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) to a pharmacist who already holds a Department controlled substance registration obtained for some other activity.
Say what the DEA limb of 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires, what qualifies it, and what the regulation leaves to the federal scheme.
List the three conditions 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) adds where prescriptive practices are included in the agreement, and say what each one is fastened to.
Distinguish the Department registration required by 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) from the controlled substance registration required by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1.
Recite the particulars a prescribing pharmacist supplies to a dispensing pharmacist under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) and identify the one no ordinary practitioner prescription carries.
Choose the correct instrument for a patient in a licensed health facility and state where the writing must be entered.
Name the boundary between this section and the separate retail collaborative practice regime.

orientation.text: Massachusetts locates a pharmacist's prescribing authority in 105 CMR 700.003, the Department of Public Health section on registration of persons for a specific activity, and the paragraph that carries the authority is 105 CMR 700.003(G). Its opening words are the whole of the power: a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, provided the following requirements are met. Two things follow from that single sentence and both are examinable. The power is three-fold, and the words as authorized in attach to each of the three acts separately rather than to the bundle. And the sentence closes on a proviso, so the numbered paragraphs that follow are not commentary on the power; they are conditions on it, and a pharmacist who fails one of them is not a pharmacist exercising a power imperfectly but a pharmacist without the power at all.

Read the three acts as three separate permissions. Issuing starts a prescription or medication order. Modifying changes one that already exists. Discontinuing stops the therapy. Nothing in the opening words ranks them by gravity, and nothing makes the smaller act a component of the larger one, so the intuition that a pharmacist trusted to change a dose must also be trusted to stop the drug has no foothold in the text. Discontinuation in particular is a regulated prescribing act and not a clinical judgement sitting outside the regulation, which is why an agreement silent on discontinuation leaves the pharmacist without authority to discontinue no matter how plainly the clinical case for stopping is made out. The other half of the opening words does comparable work on the agreement itself: the agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, three named instruments read conjunctively, so an agreement answering one of them but not the others is not an agreement this paragraph recognises.

The first of the conditions this section teaches is 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2): the pharmacist registers with the Department, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000. The load-bearing words are for the purpose of prescribing. A pharmacist may already hold a Department controlled substance registration obtained for some other activity, and the paragraph declines to treat a registration as one undifferentiated permission to handle controlled substances: the purpose for which the registration was taken out is part of the requirement, so a registration obtained so that a pharmacy could dispense does not carry prescribing authority across to a collaborating pharmacist. The federal limb is drafted differently again. It is expressly conditional, the pharmacist registering with the DEA if applicable, so it does not attach to every collaborating pharmacist merely because an agreement exists; and the regulation refers the question of when it does apply out to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 rather than answering it in its own terms, which means the answer turns on what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

A second registration requirement comes from the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and is easily conflated with the first. 247 CMR 16.02(1) sets out the qualifications a pharmacist must satisfy to enter into a collaborative practice agreement and engage in collaborative practice, and 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) adds three further conditions, but only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement. The first is to maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000. The second is to complete training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) prior to initially obtaining a controlled substance registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence. The third is to submit an attestation, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth, in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Notice what each condition is fastened to, because that is where the examinable difference sits: the registration to the term of the agreement, the training to the renewal of the pharmacist licence, and the attestation to a state of affairs the pharmacist swears to. The other qualifications listed in 247 CMR 16.02(1) apply to every collaborating pharmacist and belong to the companion section on who may practise; only subparagraph (f) is triggered by prescriptive practices.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) governs what happens when the prescription leaves the prescribing pharmacist and reaches someone who will fill it. The pharmacist may issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20, which is the general law's oral prescription provision, provided that the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies their name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides their registration number, work address, phone number, and the name of the supervising physician. Two things are clearly identified and four things are provided, and every one of the six runs to the dispensing pharmacist rather than to the patient, which is what a transmission between two pharmacists looks like. Three of the four provided particulars are the sort of thing any prescriber supplies. The work address is stated as a work address, so a home address or a mobile number offered in its place does not answer the paragraph. The distinctive particular is the last one, the name of the supervising physician, which an ordinary practitioner prescription never carries and which the pharmacist's own prescribing authority does not dispense with. Because these particulars are the proviso on which the pharmacist may issue at all, a transmission that omits one of them is incomplete rather than merely untidy, and the course open to the receiving pharmacist is to obtain the missing particular before filling rather than to weigh how material it seemed.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) deals with the opposite situation, a patient who will not be carrying a prescription to a pharmacy because the patient is inside a licensed health facility. There the pharmacist may prescribe a controlled substance for the patient through the use of a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided that such a written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000. Three elements decide questions on this paragraph. The instrument is a written medication order, not an outpatient prescription form and not an oral instruction. The place is the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, not a record the pharmacy or the pharmacist keeps and not a note left with staff. And the gate is that the facility is a licensed health facility; the paragraph names a hospital, a long term care facility, an ambulatory care clinic and a hospice, introducing them with the word including, so those four are an illustration of the class rather than the class itself, and a setting that holds no health facility licence falls outside the paragraph however carefully it maintains care records of its own.

This section is the prescribing act and nothing more. It does not decide what collaborative drug therapy management is or who may enter into an agreement, and it does not decide what the agreement document must contain; those are the subjects of the companion sections on the practice and on the agreement, and a question about qualifications, referral, consent or required agreement terms is answered there. It also stops short of the retail regime. 105 CMR 700.003(G) addresses particular settings in separate numbered paragraphs, of which the facility paragraph taught here is one, and the paragraph directed at the retail setting, together with the statutory conditions on a collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business and the schedules such a pharmacist may or may not be authorised to prescribe, is the retail section's material. Where a question turns on what a pharmacist practising in a community or retail pharmacy may prescribe, this section supplies the power, the registration and the instrument, and the schedule limits must be taken from the retail section rather than inferred from anything here.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborative practice agreement authorises a pharmacist to issue prescriptions for a referred patient's hypertension and to discontinue therapy where a listed adverse effect appears. It says nothing about changing doses. Reviewing the patient, the pharmacist concludes that the current dose should be halved rather than stopped. May she halve it?
steps: Return to the opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G): a pharmacist may issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement.
Separate the three acts. This agreement addresses issuing and discontinuing, and modifying is a distinct act rather than a lesser instance of either of them.
Resist the direction of travel in the facts. Halving a dose looks more conservative than stopping the drug, but conservatism is not the test the paragraph applies; authorisation act by act is.
Check the remaining route. Discontinuation is authorised, so stopping the drug is within the agreement, but that does not convert into a power to leave the patient on a changed dose.
worked_examples.resolution: She may not modify the dose under this agreement. The error the scenario invites is ranking the three acts by clinical gravity and assuming authority to do the graver act carries authority to do the milder one; the opening words authorise each act only as authorized in the agreement, so the agreement has to be amended before she can modify.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist holds a current Department controlled substance registration that her employer obtained years ago so that the pharmacy could dispense. She now signs a collaborative practice agreement that includes prescriptive practices and proposes to prescribe. She reasons that a controlled substance registration is a controlled substance registration. What is missing?
steps: Read 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) as a whole: the pharmacist registers with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
Test her registration against the purpose element rather than against its currency. It is current, but it was obtained for dispensing, and the purpose is part of the requirement.

Now add the Board's overlay, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

Keep the two registration requirements apart. One is a condition on the prescribing power in the Department's regulation; the other is a qualification in the Board's regulation that runs for the term of the agreement.
worked_examples.resolution: She needs Department registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and, because her agreement includes prescriptive practices, the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) as well. The error the scenario invites is treating a controlled substance registration as one undifferentiated permission, so that an instrument held for another purpose is read as covering this one.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist telephones a prescription to a pharmacy across town. She gives her name, says she is a pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement, gives her registration number, names her supervising physician, and offers her mobile number, saying she moves between sites and has no fixed work address to give. The receiving pharmacist is minded to fill it.
steps: List what 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) requires: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, and registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician provided.
Mark off what was supplied. Name, designation, registration number, supervising physician and a phone number are all present.
Identify what is absent. The paragraph specifies a work address as a particular in its own right, alongside the phone number, so a contact number does not stand in for it.
Treat the proviso as a condition on issuing rather than as a checklist of good practice, which means the transmission is incomplete as it stands.
worked_examples.resolution: The receiving pharmacist should obtain the work address before filling. The error the scenario invites is substituting one particular for another on the reasoning that the prescriber is reachable anyway, when the paragraph lists the work address and the phone number as separate items and conditions the pharmacist's power to issue on all of them being supplied.

worked_examples.scenario: A collaborating pharmacist prescribes a controlled substance for a patient of a licensed hospice under an agreement that authorises her to do so. She writes a medication order rather than a prescription, but files it in the collaborative practice file her pharmacy department keeps for the hospice, and tells the hospice nurse the order is on file. Has she used the paragraph correctly?
steps: Confirm the setting first. A hospice is among the licensed health facilities 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) names, so the paragraph is available to her.
Confirm the instrument. She wrote a medication order rather than an outpatient prescription form, which is what the paragraph calls for.
Test the location of the writing, which is the element she has got wrong: the paragraph requires the written medication order to be entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.
Note the closing condition as well, that such a written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000, so getting the instrument right does not exhaust the paragraph.
worked_examples.resolution: She has used the right instrument in the right kind of setting but has entered it in the wrong record, so the paragraph is not satisfied until the order is entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the hospice. The error the scenario invites is treating the medication order as a document the pharmacy owns and files, when the paragraph fixes both the instrument and the record it must live on.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist practises under an agreement at a licensed ambulatory care clinic, where she prescribes for referred patients by medication order. One patient is leaving the clinic and needs the same therapy dispensed by a community pharmacy near home. The pharmacist proposes to write the same medication order and let the patient take a copy to that pharmacy. What has to change, and what cannot be decided from this section?
steps: Separate the two instruments. Inside the clinic, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility.

Recognise that a prescription reaching a pharmacy for dispensing is the subject of a different paragraph, 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7), which permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20.

Attach the particulars to the second route: name and professional designation clearly identified to the dispensing pharmacist, plus registration number, work address, phone number and the supervising physician's name.

Stop before the question this section does not answer. Whether a pharmacist may prescribe this particular product for dispensing in a community or retail pharmacy depends on the separate retail regime, which is the companion section's subject.
worked_examples.resolution: The instrument must change: a facility medication order does not travel, and issuing to a dispensing pharmacy engages 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) and its particulars. The error the scenario invites is carrying an instrument that worked in one setting into another, and the further trap is trying to settle the schedule question here rather than in the retail section.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) let a pharmacist do which three things to a prescription or medication order?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Issue, modify or discontinue it, in each case as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: an agreement that authorises a pharmacist to modify a therapy also authorises the pharmacist to discontinue it.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. The three acts are stated in parallel and each is exercisable only as authorized in the agreement, so authority to modify does not carry authority to discontinue.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What do the words that close the opening sentence of 105 CMR 700.003(G) do to the numbered paragraphs beneath it?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The sentence ends provided the following requirements are met, so the numbered paragraphs are conditions on the power rather than commentary about it.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) the pharmacist registers with the Department in accordance with ______, and with the DEA ______, for the purpose of ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 105 CMR 700.004; if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300; prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A pharmacist already holds a current Department controlled substance registration obtained so her pharmacy could dispense. What does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) still require of her before she prescribes?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Registration with the Department for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000. The purpose the registration was obtained for is part of the requirement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which three conditions does 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) add, and what triggers them?
retrieval_prompts.answer: They are triggered if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement: maintain a current Department controlled substance registration during the term of the agreement; complete the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence; and submit an attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury about participation in MassHealth.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The biennial training required by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2. is a condition precedent to renewing what?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The pharmacist licence, not merely the collaborative practice agreement.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: List the particulars 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) requires the prescribing pharmacist to give the dispensing pharmacist.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Name and professional designation clearly identified, and registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician provided.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which particular in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) has no counterpart on an ordinary practitioner prescription?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The name of the supervising physician.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: For a patient in a licensed health facility, what instrument does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorise and where must it be entered?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written medication order, entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and it must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which facilities does 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) name, and is the list exhaustive?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A hospital, long term care facility, ambulatory care clinic or hospice. They are introduced by including, so they illustrate the class; the operative gate is that the facility is a licensed health facility.

quick_review.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G) opens by permitting a pharmacist to issue, modify or discontinue a prescription or medication order as authorized in a collaborative practice agreement, and closes on the words provided the following requirements are met.
Each of the three acts must be found in the agreement separately; the acts are stated in parallel, so none of them implies another.
The agreement must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 together, not one of them at the drafter's choice.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and with the DEA if applicable in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000.
A Department registration obtained for a different activity does not carry prescribing authority, because the purpose forms part of the requirement.
The DEA limb is qualified by the words if applicable, so it binds according to the federal scheme in 21 CFR 1300 and not by virtue of the collaborative practice agreement.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) attaches three conditions, and only where prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement.

Those conditions are a Department controlled substance registration maintained during the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and a sworn MassHealth attestation.
The section 18(e) training is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, which ties a prescriptive-practice condition to the licence rather than to the agreement.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) permits the pharmacist to issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 provided the prescribing pharmacist clearly identifies name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provides registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.
The particulars in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) run to the dispensing pharmacist, and the work address is listed separately from the phone number.

105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) authorises prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility through a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, provided the order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacist proposes to act on a patient's drug therapy under a collaborative practice agreement.
decision_logic.action: Name the act first: issuing, modifying or discontinuing. Then look for that act, by name, in the agreement, because 105 CMR 700.003(G) authorises each one only as authorized in the agreement.

decision_logic.condition: The agreement authorises the act, and the question is whether the pharmacist may exercise the power at all.
decision_logic.action: Treat the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as conditions, since the opening words end provided the following requirements are met, and work through the ones that bear on the facts.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacist already holds a Department controlled substance registration.
decision_logic.action: Ask what purpose it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, so a registration held for another activity does not satisfy it.

decision_logic.condition: A question asks whether the collaborating pharmacist needs DEA registration.
decision_logic.action: Do not answer yes or no on the strength of the agreement. The limb applies if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, so ask what the pharmacist will actually prescribe.

Add the three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f): the controlled substance registration maintained during the term, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training before initially obtaining that registration and at least biennially thereafter, and the sworn MassHealth attestation.

decision_logic.condition: The prescription is being transmitted to a pharmacist who will dispense it.
decision_logic.action: Check the transmission against the list in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) item by item, and where a particular is missing, obtain it rather than assess how material it was.

decision_logic.condition: The patient is in a facility.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the facility is a licensed health facility. If it is, use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8); if it is not, that paragraph does not supply the instrument.

decision_logic.condition: The question turns on which schedules a pharmacist in a community or retail pharmacy may prescribe.
decision_logic.action: Stop. This section supplies the power, the registration and the instrument; the retail regime and its controlled substance limits are the retail section's material.

ma_vs_federal.text: 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) makes a federal registration part of a Massachusetts condition: the pharmacist registers with the Department and with the DEA, if applicable, in accordance with 21 CFR 1300. Massachusetts therefore treats the federal registration as one of the conditions on its own prescribing power rather than leaving it to federal enforcement alone.

The federal limb is incorporated conditionally. The regulation does not itself state when DEA registration is applicable; it refers that question to 21 CFR 1300, so the Massachusetts requirement is as wide, and no wider, as the federal scheme makes it.

exceptions.text: The DEA limb of 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) applies only if applicable, so it is not a universal precondition of prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement.

The three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) bite only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement; an agreement without prescriptive practices does not attract them.

The medication order route in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) is available only where the patient is in a licensed health facility, so the instrument it authorises is unavailable in a setting that holds no such licence.

timing_deadlines.event: Pharmacist exercises the prescribing power under a collaborative practice agreement
timing_deadlines.timeframe: The Department registration must be held, for the purpose of prescribing, at the time the power is exercised
timing_deadlines.consequence: Without a registration taken out for that purpose the condition in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is unmet and the power in 105 CMR 700.003(G) is not available.

timing_deadlines.event: Agreement including prescriptive practices is in force
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Throughout the term of the agreement
timing_deadlines.consequence: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. requires a current Department controlled substance registration to be maintained for the whole term, so allowing it to lapse mid-term breaks the qualification.

timing_deadlines.event: Training required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Before initially obtaining the controlled substance registration, and at least biennially thereafter
timing_deadlines.consequence: Completion is a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2., so the consequence of missing it falls on the licence and not only on the agreement.

forms_records.text: The collaborative practice agreement is the instrument that authorises the prescribing act, and it must meet the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. Each of issuing, modifying and discontinuing must appear in it before the pharmacist may do that thing.

A Department registration obtained in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000 is the instrument 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires; the purpose recorded for it is part of what makes it sufficient.
A DEA registration in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 is required by the same paragraph where the federal limb is applicable.

Where prescriptive practices are included, a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department, held pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000, must be maintained during the term of the agreement.

Where prescriptive practices are included, the pharmacist submits an attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury that the pharmacist participates in, or had applied to participate in, MassHealth as either a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

A prescription issued under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) is issued in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 and carries with it, to the dispensing pharmacist, the prescribing pharmacist's name and professional designation, registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

For a patient in a licensed health facility the instrument is a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and that written order must meet all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing under a collaborative practice agreement
role_duties.duty: Exercise only those of the three acts, issuing, modifying and discontinuing, that the agreement authorises, and treat the numbered requirements in 105 CMR 700.003(G) as conditions on the power rather than as guidance.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist seeking to prescribe under 105 CMR 700.003(G)
role_duties.duty: Register with the Department in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004 for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000, and with the DEA in accordance with 21 CFR 1300 where that limb is applicable.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist whose agreement includes prescriptive practices
role_duties.duty: Maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department for the whole term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000.

role_duties.role: Pharmacist obtaining or renewing a controlled substance registration for prescriptive practice
role_duties.duty: Complete the training required pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) before initially obtaining the registration and at least biennially thereafter, this being a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence.

Submit the MassHealth participation attestation signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, the attestation covering either participation as a provider of services or the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

role_duties.role: Prescribing pharmacist transmitting a prescription for another pharmacy to fill
role_duties.duty: Clearly identify name and professional designation to the dispensing pharmacist and provide registration number, work address, phone number and the name of the supervising physician.

role_duties.role: Dispensing pharmacist receiving a prescription from a collaborating pharmacist
role_duties.duty: Check the transmission against the particulars 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) lists, and where one is missing, obtain it, since the particulars are the proviso on which the prescribing pharmacist may issue at all.

Be identified by name in the particulars the prescribing pharmacist supplies to the dispensing pharmacist, so the physician's identity travels with each prescription the pharmacist issues under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7).

role_duties.role: Pharmacist prescribing for a patient in a licensed health facility
role_duties.duty: Use a written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, and make sure that written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

common_traps.text: Ranking issuing, modifying and discontinuing by clinical gravity and assuming the greater authority includes the lesser. The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) state the three acts in parallel and authorise each one only as authorized in the agreement.
Treating a decision to stop a therapy as a clinical judgement outside the regulation. Discontinuation is one of the three regulated prescribing acts.
Reading the numbered paragraphs of 105 CMR 700.003(G) as descriptive detail. The opening sentence ends provided the following requirements are met, which makes them conditions.
Accepting an existing controlled substance registration whatever it was obtained for. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) requires registration for the purpose of prescribing.
Applying the DEA limb uniformly, either requiring it of every collaborating pharmacist or dismissing it as boilerplate. It is qualified by the words if applicable and points to 21 CFR 1300.

Merging the two registration requirements. The Department registration in 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2) is a condition on the prescribing power; the controlled substance registration in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. is a qualification that must be maintained for the term of the agreement.

Attaching the section 18(e) training to the agreement. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)2. makes it a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence, and it is required before the registration is first obtained as well as at least biennially thereafter.

Supplying the particulars an ordinary prescriber would give and omitting the supervising physician's name, or offering a callback number in place of the work address. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(7) lists both, separately.

Writing an outpatient prescription for a facility inpatient, or entering the medication order on a record the pharmacy keeps. 105 CMR 700.003(G)(8) fixes both the instrument and the record it must be entered on.
Transplanting the facility medication order into a setting that holds no health facility licence because its records look similar. The paragraph is framed for a patient in a licensed health facility.
